The bull case rests on the third quarter of fiscal 2026, when revenue of 1.85 billion dollars rose 36.54% from a year earlier and net income of 397 million dollars rose 107.85% [D1]. Both reporting segments grew, with Communications Solutions Group revenue of 1.35 billion dollars up 43.09% and Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue of 501 million dollars up 21.60%, and segment income from operations of 613 million dollars up 81.36% [D1]. The guide for the next report is revenue of 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion dollars, which management said represents growth of about 37% at the mid-point, and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 dollars on a weighted diluted share count of about 172 million shares [D1]. Management said demand is far exceeding its ability to supply and called the supply chain the governor of near-term revenue, which frames that guide as a supply number rather than a demand number [D3]. Management expects orders slightly up from the third quarter, said the pipeline continues to grow strongly, and called the 6G opportunity larger than the 5G cycle [D3]. What the bull case needs to see at the next report is revenue at or above the top of the guided range of 1.95 billion dollars and earnings per share at or above 3.40 dollars [D1].

The bear case points to costs rising alongside revenue, with cost of products and services of 630 million dollars up 21.62%, research and development of 312 million dollars up 24.8% and selling, general and administrative of 446 million dollars up 25.99% [D1]. Management cautioned that the one-time tariff impacts this year artificially lifted fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat [D3]. Management also said supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue for the next several quarters and that the supply situation is likely to be nonlinear [D3]. The mix of the wireline business has shifted toward manufacturing from research and development as AI data centre build-outs scale [D4]. Acquisition integration is now largely complete, including systems migrations, one quarter ahead of schedule [D3]. What the bear case needs to see at the next report is revenue below the bottom of the guided range of 1.93 billion dollars or earnings per share below 3.34 dollars [D1].
